A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from OMG to OMatG. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated material and changed experimental conditions.

before.justification: v1 reports original crystal structure prediction experiments on four datasets and de novo generation experiments with validity, structural, and stability results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds interpolant studies, DFT evaluations, LLM-initialized generation experiments, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: v1 fixes lattice interpolation to linear with zero latent noise and uses a fixed encoder-decoder switch time. v2 implements and evaluates varied lattice interpolants, generalized encoder-decoder paths, and variance-exploding diffusion interpolants. Appendix E also introduces OMatG-LLM, which refines LLM-generated initial structures. These extend the generation procedure beyond the naming change.

E1.justification: The four main datasets and the CSP/DNG tasks remain. Appendix E adds an LLM-generated crystal dataset and an evaluation scenario using structures from a fine-tuned Llama-70B model as initial inputs. This extends coverage within the existing inorganic-crystal domain. Carbon-24 remains excluded in both versions.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates DiffCSP and FlowMM, while citing MatterGen results with an explicit comparability caveat. v2 directly evaluates MatterGen-MP in Tables II–III and XII and the structural analyses. Appendix E additionally evaluates FlowLLM against OMatG-LLM, substantially broadening the actual comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 adds DFT relaxation of 1,000 structures for the main stability comparison; v1 relies on MatterSim relaxation of filtered sets generated from 10,000 samples. MatterSim results remain separately reported in v2. Niggli reduction becomes a tuned preprocessing option, whereas v1 explicitly excludes it from tuning. New LLM experiments and controlled GPU timing tests introduce additional evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: v2 expands the selected-model comparisons into systematic studies of positional interpolants, ODE versus SDE sampling, and latent noise for perov-5 CSP, MP-20 CSP, and MP-20 DNG (Tables VI–XI). It also adds MatterSim-versus-DFT agreement analysis and computational-cost comparisons. The existing matching-tolerance analysis in Figure 7 is retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Tables XIV–XV newly report training and sampling times with ± values. Neither the uncertainty statistic nor the repetition count is specified. The main CSP and DNG quality results still lack reported confidence intervals or variability across seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive CSP, DNG, DFT, LLM, and timing results. The 83.06% perov-5 match rate for VP SBD is new, while v1's 80.85% trigonometric result is retained in Table VI. DiffCSP's reported MatterSim RMSD changes from 1.295 Å in v1 Table III to 0.367 Å in v2 Table XII. The new main-table stability scores use DFT and should not be interpreted as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's basic interpolant definitions and losses, v2 Appendix B2 formally generalizes the encoder-decoder interpolant through switch-time, variance, and exponent parameters. Appendix B9 adds derivations connecting stochastic interpolants to VP and VE diffusion, including time transformations and linear, cosine, constant, and geometric noise schedules. These are substantive mathematical additions.

C1.justification: The central claim of a unifying stochastic-interpolant framework achieving state-of-the-art CSP and DNG performance remains. Introduction I B extends the explicit DNG superiority claim from DiffCSP and FlowMM to MatterGen. This broadens a specific claimed comparison without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 expands the perov-5 explanation to distinguish chemical-environment matching from geometric symmetry and qualifies v1's coordinate-loss dominance claim with lattice-dominated exceptions. Appendix B10 explains why species modeling alone cannot explain CSP gains over FlowMM. New qualifications limit the manifold construction to flat tori and distinguish qualitative MatterSim trends from quantitative conclusions requiring DFT.

D1.justification: v1 gives a short list of tuned quantities; v2 supplies search distributions, selected hyperparameters, tuning-trial counts, and cross-dataset hyperparameter-transfer details. It also documents the diffusion coefficient, fingerprint implementations, Atomate2 DFT workflow, LLM data sources, and timing hardware/settings. An explicit OMatG repository link is added. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: The central related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain. v2 adds references on rectified flow, diffusion schedules, FlowLLM, and LLM-based crystal generation. Appendices B9–B10 and E explain the framework's relationship to FlowMM, diffusion models, and LLM refinement more explicitly, including architectural differences from FlowMM.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: coupling and velocity annealing move to the appendix, Section V gains separate results and discussion subsections, and the conclusion is rewritten. Methodological explanations and appendix organization are extensively expanded, including an acronym glossary. Terminology is refined, notably distinguishing velocity from drift, alongside the OMG-to-OMatG rename.

P2.justification: Table I expands from one selected OMG row to multiple named variants, and stability tables gain a novelty column and additional comparators. v2 adds paired results/hyperparameter tables and LLM and timing tables. Figures 3 and 8 are redrawn, while Figures 9–12 expand to include MatterGen-MP and VE-SBD panels. Core explanatory figures and Figure 7 are largely retained.

improvement.justification: DFT validation and direct MatterGen-MP evaluation address v1's reliance on a learned potential and its explicitly limited MatterGen comparison. Systematic variant studies and detailed implementation reporting substantially strengthen evidential support and reproducibility. The DFT evaluation uses fewer structures, timing uncertainties remain undefined, and Eq. C9 has an apparent validity-direction inconsistency in its minimized objective. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial validation and documentation gains.
